plan.change: Create quantity.mjs at repo root as an ES module. Read all of stdin, trim it, then parse with `const n = parseInt(input, 10);` and check `Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0`. If true, print JSON.stringify({quantity: n}) to stdout; otherwise print JSON.stringify({error: "invalid_quantity"}). This is the first candidate implementation, using parseInt on the trimmed input to accept positive integers.
plan.verification: Independent protected verification will run the pinned test/quantity.test.mjs via npm test to check behavior against the fixture contract, including the fractional-input case (e.g. '1.5').
plan.assumptions: parseInt-based parsing is expected to be accepted for integer-looking positive inputs but will incorrectly accept the leading-numeric portion of fractional strings like '1.5' (parseInt('1.5',10) === 1), so the protected fractional-input check is expected to fail for this first candidate, per the qualification design.
